triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 05 composition defined entry_is_line_a..e as equality tests against five exemplar statistical reporting numbers from other chapters, grounding chapter-05 §301 / §122 / reciprocal-exclusion gating on provisions outside this chapter's scope so those branches could never fire for any line chapter 05 actually covers.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 0: identical two-hunk diff (summary + removal of the five entry_is_line_* derived rules). Diff read individually; justification reused from index 0.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute the reading and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are equality tests against statistical reporting numbers belonging to chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85 (`(hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")` … `(hts_number == "8541.42.00.10")`), each carrying its own proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions, from a chapter-01 composition. Those flags were the sole grounding for chapter-01 legal-category rules — `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (9903.01.32 annex list) had `formula: entry_is_line_a`, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (9903.01.33 metals scope) had `formula: entry_is_line_b`, and the §301 China stack and the 9903.05.07 carve-out branch `(if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 …)` all turn on them — so chapter-01 duty gating was grounded on provisions outside this chapter's scope, and the PR calls that coupling out as having "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins." This is not mechanical: formulas, proof atoms and the module's input/output surface changed (the PR ledger records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs"), and it is the removal arm of untraceable_branch (a condition with no basis in the cited source / grounded on the wrong provision), not a boundary, amount, period or polarity error.

triage.verifier_notes: inferred from verified sibling module index 0 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) The module's own summary still asserts "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values … runtime semantics are unchanged" — that is generator boilerplate and is contradicted by the diff, which removes formulas and proof atoms; do not treat it as a denial. (2) Every consuming formula (`entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, the §301 slots, §338 gate) is byte-identical before and after; this commit changes only where the flags come from (local derived rule → caller input under the referenced-implies-input convention). If a reviewer scores "meaning change" strictly as a change to surviving formula text, this commit alone looks like an input-surface refactor and the case slides toward unclear. (3) The repair is partial in this file: `entry_is_energy_resource` (cited to 9903.01.13 energy/critical minerals) still reads `- formula: (hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")` at post line 1950, and the other-chapter citation paths remain in `source_verification.corpus_citation_paths`, so the same exemplar-grounding defect survives the commit for at least one rule. (4) The full membership-semantic regating (`entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered`) and the new §232 steel component land in sibling commits of PR #1300, so the PR quote in the first reader's justification describes the stacked change, not literally this diff. Verified read-only via `git show` of parent 956a5474 and 2a6bdb01de; no provision lookup was needed because the defect is structural (wrong-chapter grounding), not text-dependent.
